props.eyebrow: Build by hand · Two native containers
props.title: Build a page yourself
props.lead: You can also create projects and pages in the workbench without an agent. A Page arranges content in reading order for documents, reports and web pages; a Board lets you pan, zoom, draw and place objects freely. You can nest either inside the other in the same file.

content.text: has an agent build your first interface; this page shows how to do it yourself, without an agent. Both give you the same kind of page, and either way an agent can keep working on it later.

steps.title: New project
steps.body: Click New project in the sidebar and enter a name. A project groups related pages, folders, components and templates; for example, create one for “Literature reading” and another for “Product research”.
steps.result: The project appears in the sidebar, empty.

steps.title: Add a Page or Board
steps.body: Click **+** in the top-left corner, or open a folder's New menu, and choose “Blank page” or “Board”. Use a Page for articles, notes and reports; use a Board to place things freely or draw relationship diagrams.

steps.title: Enter the content and insert the component with `/`
steps.body: On a Page, type text directly, or type `/` to search for and insert tables, charts, images and other components; you can keep editing their settings after inserting them. On a Board, press `/` on an empty area, or right-click and choose Add component…
steps.result: The component appears at the cursor position, and the text before and after it remains unchanged.

steps.title: Confirm saved
steps.body: The workbench saves automatically; you can also press `Cmd+S` (macOS) or `Ctrl+S` (Windows / Linux).
steps.result: The save status shows “Saved on this device”.

Use Page to write content that people can read along; use Board to write content that needs to be placed, compared, and circled. If you are unsure, start with Page and embed a Board in the area that requires spatial relationship.

content.text: Page and Board are listed in the component library like Markdown, pictures, and charts, and the search, preview, and insertion methods are exactly the same.
Open the insert menu and directly search for the component name, such as "whiteboard" and "mind map". The insertion position is where the cursor is, and the text before and after remains intact.
, or right-click and select "Add Component..."; double-click the blank space to write text directly, P brush, R rectangle.
Add a shell to existing content
: Select "Put to Page" or "Put to Board" in the container operation menu. The original node becomes a child node of the new container, and the identity and content remain unchanged.
You can continue typing in a normal blank paragraph at the end of the page. Existing sequences, grids, and free groups can still be edited and switched in "Region Layout" in "Module Settings".
The outer frame belongs to the parent, and the layout belongs to yourself.
Each embedded container has two levels of settings:
The parent determines its position and outline
It decides how to arrange it internally
. Click on the nodes in the picture below to see what they control.

nodes.label: Root Page
nodes.detail: The outermost layer of the page. It has no parent frame, the child content is arranged in order, and the reader scrolls vertically.

nodes.label: Text and components
nodes.detail: Body text, text modules, and streaming content share the same editor, and cursor, selection, and keyboard navigation can continue through them. Hovering or selecting will not frame the content.

nodes.label: Embedded Board
nodes.detail: The parent Page gives it a window with a fixed height. No matter how large the interior is, the article will not be stretched. There is a read lock in the upper right corner when embedding, and it is locked by default.

nodes.label: Page in Board
nodes.detail: Board positions it using local coordinates. The default is a fixed reading window, which can be read up and down; it can be changed to "Grows with content" in "Module Settings → Height Mode".

nodes.label: painting
nodes.detail: Only belongs to the Board. The stroke points are saved according to the local coordinates of its own outer frame. Zooming in and out of the parent will not rewrite the strokes. Arrows can be bound to objects at the same level, and the endpoints follow when the object moves.

nodes.label: components
nodes.detail: The position and frame of components on the Board are also determined by the Board; clicks on the selected components are handled by the components themselves.

Use the frame handles to move the entire module, and text or internal controls to edit content. Cross-container movement, deletion, painting, and wrapping can be undone; personal scrolling, camera positions, and selections are only saved locally and do not count as content modifications.

: Click the object to select it, hold down any position and drag to move it; click the selected text again to enter editing (you can also press Enter), Escape to exit editing and keep it selected. Dragging in the blank area is a box selection.

content.text: Reading lock: scroll the page or operate the content inside

Zoomable content embedded in the page will compete with page scrolling. Reading Lock solves this problem: when locked, scrolling is handed over to the outer page, and clicks, right-clicks, prompts, and inner editing controls work as usual.
